explanation: Your first pick is right only 1 time in 3. The host never opens the car's door, so in the other 2 cases out of 3, the car is behind the door left closed.

claims.text: In the Monty Hall problem, when the host knowingly opens another door to show a goat, switching wins the car with probability 2/3, about 67%.
Switching wins with probability 2/3, not 25%, 33% or 50%; 33% is the chance of winning by staying with the first pick.
The contestant's first pick hides the car with probability 1/3.
In the other 2 out of 3 cases, the car is behind the remaining closed door, because the host never reveals the car.
